notes: Domestic channels (task 2, Phase D): the route framework grows from four to seven adapters — DingTalk, Feishu and WeChat join Discord/Slack/Email/Webhook — plus an explicit outbound trigger for routes without an inbound path. (1) Route directions are honest per platform: DingTalk sends through a custom-robot webhook (optional HMAC-SHA256 sign over a millisecond timestamp, appended as timestamp/sign query parameters; the response body is checked for errcode even on HTTP 200; the target is a label — the webhook URL decides the group) with no inbound, because this platform delivers robot messages only through its stream protocol or a callback to a publicly reachable URL and this console is loopback-only; WeChat sends official-account customer-service messages (appid/secret slots -> cached access_token -> custom/send to an openid target) with no inbound, which would require a certified service account and a public callback URL; Feishu is full-duplex on one self-built app identity — tenant token cached module-wide and refreshed 120s before expiry, send via im/v1/messages with the chat id as target, and inbound via single-page chat-history polling with a raw-timestamp cursor (unit-defense for ms vs seconds, boundary-id dedup so same-instant arrivals deliver exactly once, start_time always sent in seconds, fresh polls deliver the current batch). Feishu token-invalid codes invalidate the cache and retry exactly once; quota codes fail honestly without retry. WeChat content is capped at 1024 bytes with UTF-8-safe truncation, only errcode is ever surfaced (error hints can embed secret fragments), 45015 fails honestly, and token-rejection codes retry once. (2) Outbound triggers so these routes are never dead code: POST /api/channels/send on the loopback console (Bearer WEB_TOKEN; 400 validation, 409 disabled/unconfigured naming only the missing slot, 502 delivery failure with details kept server-side, 200 accepted) and mycore.scheduler --origin now accepts route:target strings alongside integer chat ids for cron delivery through a domestic route (malformed origins exit rc=2 with one honest line). The service loop, allowlist gate and cron origin chain from the previous release are reused unchanged. (3) Zero credential echo everywhere: configured() failures name slots, and no log, exception or API response carries a slot value. Verified before these notes were written: the offline suite grew to 645/645 (57 new domestic-route checks; previous counts unchanged) and console smoke to 87/87 (endpoint gates and new-partition validation); an E2E script ran 44 checks to completion against local HTTP sinks — real wire shapes for all three outbound routes including server-side HMAC recomputation of the DingTalk sign, the Feishu token/send/poll dialogues across three incremental polls, the WeChat token/send dialogue with a planted secret proving errmsg never surfaces, and the console endpoint end-to-end through the live web process — with settings and secrets restored byte-for-byte. External connectivity to the real DingTalk/Feishu/WeChat services remains pending credentials and is claimed nowhere. Also in this release: docs/features/channels_domestic.md documents the protocol contracts and the per-route honest boundaries; site badges and handover gate tables re-synced to the new counts.
